title: The Violin in Washington Square
synopsis: By the white arch, musicians play every afternoon.
One of them knows Eleanor's old song.
You must reach her before the TV crew does.
goal: Find the violin girl, earn her trust and learn her family's secret.

options.label: The guitar player
options.feedback: A guitar has strings. But is it played with a bow?
options.altText: a young man playing a guitar with his fingers, no bow

options.label: The violin player
options.altText: a young woman in a green beret playing a violin with a bow, the violin under her chin

options.label: The cello player
options.feedback: Strings and a bow, yes. But a cello stands on the floor, not under the chin.
options.altText: an old man playing a big cello with a bow, the cello standing on the floor

notes: A picture choice with the names hidden: Eleanor's spare note (strings, a bow) and Maya's line (under the chin); the guitar has no bow, the cello is not under the chin. Three scenes by the white arch, one musician each; the violinist is drawn from Rosa's portrait (a reference).

clueInputs.note: Eleanor's family plays the song on strings, with a bow.
The violin girl plays by the white arch.

learning.objective: 'on strings, with a bow', 'under the chin'을 읽고 세 연주자 중 맞는 악기를 연주하는 사람을 고른다.
expressions: My family plays my song on strings, with a bow.

play.title: Three Musicians
story: It is 3 PM. The white arch shines in the sun.
Three musicians play around the fountain.
The TV crew comes at four. There is no time to lose.
play.letterIntro: Eleanor's spare note and Maya say:
play.letter:
ELEANOR: My family plays my song on strings, with a bow.
MAYA: And the violin is small. It sits under the chin.
play.question: Which musician plays Eleanor's song?
hints: Look for strings AND a bow.
Where does each one sit: on the floor, or under the chin?
transition: It is Rosa, the violinist from Grand Central.
She plays the same slow, old tune.
When she sees you, she stops.

clue.title: The Violinist
clue.value: STRINGS · A BOW · UNDER THE CHIN
clue.note: The violin girl is Rosa Diaz. She plays the same old song everywhere on the trail.

evidence.name: Rosa's Tune
evidence.description: The slow, old song Rosa plays every day.
evidence.inscription: Heard at Grand Central and by the white arch.

discovery.title: THE SAME OLD TUNE
discovery.detail: Rosa played it at Grand Central too. Was she watching the trail?

options.label: Because you are on TV.
options.feedback: Grandma Ana says never tell strangers. What will the careful reader bring?

options.label: Because you have Eleanor's brass egg.
Because you paid her.
options.feedback: Grandma Ana says never sell it. Read who Rosa may play for.

notes: Rosa asks to see what Eleanor's first friend gave you (the brass egg, Case 02): the recall. Letter: Grandma Ana's note in Rosa's violin case, with the song's last half (D, A, D).

clueInputs.note: Rosa asks for what Eleanor's first friend gave you: the brass egg.
The last three notes stay with Eleanor's family.

learning.objective: 할머니의 쪽지에서 'a careful reader will bring Eleanor's brass egg'를 읽고 로사가 탐정을 믿는 이유를 찾는다.
expressions: Our family keeps the end of Eleanor's song.
a careful reader will bring Eleanor's brass egg

play.title: Rosa's Test
story: "Everyone wants my song today," she says.
"Show me what Eleanor's first friend gave you."
play.letterIntro: Rosa takes a note from her violin case:
play.letter:
To my Rosa,
Our family keeps the end of Eleanor's song: D, A, D.
Never sell it. Never tell strangers.
One day, a careful reader will bring Eleanor's brass egg.
For that reader, and only that reader, play the whole song.
— Grandma Ana
play.question: Why does Rosa trust you?
hints: What will the careful reader bring?
Look at what you showed Rosa from your Notebook.
transition: Rosa smiles for the first time.
"The end of the song is D, A, D," she says.
"Now I can tell you who I am."

clue.title: The Last Three Notes
clue.note: The end of Eleanor's song, kept by her family: D, A, D.

evidence.name: Grandma Ana's Note
evidence.description: A note from Rosa's grandmother, kept in her violin case.
evidence.inscription: Our family keeps the end of Eleanor's song: D, A, D.

recall.title: Show Rosa
recall.prompt: Which thing in your Notebook did Eleanor's first friend give you?
recall.miss: That is not from the Lost and Found. What did Grace give you?

discovery.title: THE END OF THE SONG
discovery.detail: D, A, D. With E, G, G, you now know the whole song.

notes: Letter: Rosa's family tree. Karl's photo (Case 05) showed baby Ruth; Rosa is Ruth's granddaughter. The helper's secret, revealed.

clueInputs.note: Karl's photo: Eleanor and her baby, Ruth.

learning.objective: 가계도(daughter, mother's grandmother)를 읽고 엘리너가 로사의 증조할머니(great-grandmother)임을 단어로 쓴다.
expressions: So Eleanor is my mother's grandmother.

play.title: Rosa's Secret
story: Rosa sits on the edge of the fountain.
She draws a little family tree in Maya's notebook.
Otto comes running across the square.
play.letter:
Eleanor Hart had a daughter, Ruth.
Ruth had a daughter, Ana.
Ana had a daughter: me, Rosa.
So Eleanor is my mother's grandmother.
Your mother's grandmother is your great-grandmother.
play.question: What is Eleanor to Rosa? Finish the sentence.
hints: Read the last line of the family tree.
Your mother's mother is one step back. Eleanor is one more step back.
transition: "Baby Ruth in Karl's photo was my grandma's mother," Rosa says.
"I played our song on the trail to watch over it."

feedback.MOTHER: Eleanor is further back than Rosa's mother. Read the tree again.
feedback.AUNT: An aunt is not in this tree. Count back: Rosa, Ana, Ruth, Eleanor.

clue.title: Rosa's Secret
clue.note: Rosa Diaz is Eleanor Hart's great-granddaughter. Her family keeps the song's end.

evidence.name: Rosa's Family Tree
evidence.description: Rosa's family tree, drawn in Maya's notebook.

lines.text: Grandma said the Lark is for a child of the city.
Not for us. So I kept quiet.
And you watched the trail with your song.
Yes. I hoped the right reader would hear it.

discovery.title: ELEANOR'S FAMILY
discovery.detail: Rosa kept quiet to keep Eleanor's promise. The Lark is for a child of the city.

notes: Rosa's 1926 music box opens with the family's old name, the name on the building where Eleanor made her toys (Otto's letter, Case 05). Inside the lid: a big wheel by the sea, the way to Case 09.

clueInputs.note: Otto's letter: Eleanor made her toys in the Hart Building.

learning.objective: 'our family's old name, the name on the building'을 읽고 하트 빌딩의 이름으로 글자를 맞춘다.
expressions: It opens with our family's old name.
the name on the building where Eleanor made her toys

play.title: Rosa's Music Box
story: Rosa takes a small wooden box from her bag.
"Eleanor made this music box in 1926," she says.
"It has a letter lock. I will let you open it."
play.letter:
My music box is locked. It opens with our family's old name.
My name is Diaz now. But a long time ago, it was different.
It is the name on the building where Eleanor made her toys.
play.question: Spell the word that opens Rosa's music box.
hints: Otto's letter talks about the building. What is it called?
play.successMessage: The music box opens and plays!
transition: E, G, G, D, A, D. The whole song plays at last.
Inside the lid is a tiny painting: a big wheel by the sea.
Then a TV truck stops at the edge of the park.
play.orderFeedback: The four tiles fit. What is the name of Eleanor's building?

evidence.name: Rosa's Music Box
evidence.description: Eleanor's 1926 music box, kept by her family. It plays the Lark's whole song.
evidence.inscription: Inside the lid: a big wheel by the sea.

ending.text: A big wheel by the sea... Coney Island!
ending.speaker: maya_chen

ending.text: The first half was on the bird: E, G, G.
Yesterday Dexter Vance offered me money for this box.
ending.speaker: rosa_diaz

ending.text: I said no. He did not smile then.
ending.speaker: rosa_diaz

ending.text: Dexter waves from the truck. His boots have little stars.

hook: Rosa's music box shows a wheel by the sea. And Dexter Vance wants that box. Why?

intro: Washington Square Park. A white arch, a fountain and music everywhere.
The TV crew will come at four.
play.caseSummary: The violin girl is Rosa. She played the same song at Grand Central. She trusted you because you carry the brass egg. Her family keeps the song's end: D, A, D. Rosa is Eleanor's great-granddaughter. Her music box opened with HART and showed a wheel by the sea.

notes: Act 2's turning point: the helper's secret. Rosa is Eleanor's great-granddaughter; she watched the trail with her song and kept Eleanor's promise.
The music box (s4_ep08_e4) is stolen in Case 10 and found in Dexter's safe in Case 11. D, A, D (s4_ep08_c2) is paid off in Case 10 and Case 12.
